sources.entry: Gaphor - Gaphor is the simple modeling tool for UML and SysML.

summary.one_liner: Gaphor is an open-source UML and SysML modeling application written in Python, with a GTK-based GUI and a scriptable library interface.
summary.what_it_does: Gaphor lets you create UML 2 and SysML models through a diagram-based GUI, and the README says it implements a fully-compliant UML 2 data model rather than just drawing pictures. The greeter dialog offers Generic, UML, SysML, RAAML and C4 Model templates, and Gaphor selects a matching profile automatically. Elements are placed from a toolbox onto a diagram and also appear in a Model Browser. The README says the GUI uses GTK and Cairo for rendering. It can also be used as a library from scripts and Jupyter notebooks to work with models programmatically. Generating diagrams from source code and generating code from diagrams are stated non-goals.
use_cases: programmatically build UML models from Python scripts
how_to_run: Download installers for macOS or Windows from the gaphor.org website
Install the Python package from PyPI
See the Installation section of the project documentation to develop Gaphor
notable: Fully-compliant UML 2 data model, not just a drawing tool
Supports UML, SysML, RAAML and C4 Model templates
Usable as a library from scripts and Jupyter notebooks
caveats: Does not generate UML diagrams from source code or source code from diagrams (stated non-goals)
Does not provide fUML or ALF execution artifacts (stated non-goal)
